\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}
\usepackage{hyperref}

\title{The Northmoor Dialect Corpus: Release Notes}
\author{Fieldwork Consortium}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Overview}
The corpus comprises 214 hours of sociolinguistic interviews
recorded between 2019 and 2023 across seventeen parishes.
Speakers were sampled by age, sex, and occupation following
the stratification used in the 1987 survey, so that the two
collections can be compared directly. Audio is distributed
as 16-bit WAV at 44.1 kHz, and transcriptions follow the
orthographic conventions described in the project manual.

\section{Annotation}
Every transcript is time-aligned at the utterance level and
carries part-of-speech tags produced by the consortium tagger
and corrected by hand. Approximately one fifth of the
material also carries phonetic transcription in X-SAMPA.
The annotation scheme is versioned, and the release ships
with a validation report that lists every file, its tagger
version, and the identity of the human corrector.

\section{File Formats}
Transcripts are distributed as plain text with one utterance
per line, prefixed by the speaker code and the time offset.
The phonetic tier, where present, is interleaved between
orthographic lines and marked by a leading percent sign in
the source files. Validation reports are comma-separated
and use the file naming scheme of the audio archive.

\section{Access}
The audio and the aligned transcripts are distributed under
the consortium licence to registered users. Registration is
free for academic use and is approved within one working
day; commercial users should contact the consortium office
before downloading. The annotated concordance lines are
archived at \url{https://example.com/a_b%20c} and are
regenerated nightly from the master annotation store, so
the snapshot always reflects the latest corrections.
Users who mirror the archive are asked to keep the version
stamp intact so that bug reports can be matched to the
exact state of the annotation store.

\section{Errata}
Three interviews from the 2021 season were transcribed with
an earlier tagger version than stated in the manual; the
affected files are listed in the validation report and will
be re-annotated in the next release. The parish of Kirkby
Underdale was mis-coded as urban in the 2022 metadata; the
correct classification is rural-agricultural, and analyses
that stratify by settlement type should be re-run.
A small number of utterances at the ends of three tapes
were truncated by a faulty memory card; the affected spans
are silent in the audio and are marked as such in the
transcripts. No replacement recordings are planned.
\end{document}
